subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should OpenClaw preserve `reason: "target-none"` as the machine-readable heartbeat skip reason and add a human-facing disabled-delivery hint, or rename the reason string itself?
rationale: The implementation is small, but the exposed reason string may already be consumed by scripts or log parsers, and the safer alternative adds a new optional diagnostic field.

options.title: Add hint, keep reason
options.body: Keep `target-none` as the stable machine reason and render an optional disabled-delivery hint in heartbeat status output.

options.title: Rename reason
options.body: Change the machine reason to `delivery-disabled` and accept the compatibility risk for consumers that parse the old value.

options.title: Leave current output
options.body: Keep the raw diagnostic unchanged and accept the operator confusion as low-priority friction.

recommendation.title: Add hint, keep reason
recommendation.body: Keep `target-none` as the stable machine reason and render an optional disabled-delivery hint in heartbeat status output.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the default-none heartbeat behavior and have the strongest history on the affected heartbeat/status contract.
